source_caption:
“I am not going to bury my son. My son is going to bury me.” 💔

John Q (2002) was one of the most personal films Nick Cassavetes ever directed. Inspired by the real-life medical struggles of his daughter Sasha, who was born with a congenital heart defect, the film carries an emotional authenticity that extends far beyond its gripping story. Cassavetes would later revisit similar themes in My Sister’s Keeper (2009), once again drawing from his family’s experiences.

While many viewers remember John Q for its powerful criticism of the American healthcare system, the filmmakers have said the story is ultimately about faith, hope, and the possibility of miracles. Denzel Washington’s deeply committed performance gives the film its emotional core, making it one of the most moving dramas of the early 2000s.

source_details.synopsis: John Q. is a 2002 American thriller crime drama film directed by Nick Cassavetes, and written by James Kearns. It stars Denzel Washington as the title character, a man who takes a hospital emergency room hostage in order for his son to receive a heart transplant. Robert Duvall, James Woods, Anne Heche, Kimberly Elise, and Ray Liotta appear in supporting roles. The film was released by New Line Cinema on February 15, 2002. It received generally negative reviews from critics, but was a commercial success, grossing $102.2 million on a $36 million budget.
